items.title: Why Urgent Security Fixes Aren't Fixed. Observe, Prove, Act, Confirm Gets Them Moving
items.snippet: The alert is critical. The fix is known. And the ticket sits in a queue for days. Security teams understand the risk, but the people who keep applications available need proof that the change won’t break anything. Their concerns are practical. Because a shell parses the whole line, an option value containing shell syntax is executed as a command by any `nx` command that constructs the project graph. Anyone who clones a hostile repository, or who checks out a pull request tha…

items.snippet: `Joi.string().email({ multiple: true })` takes quadratic time to split a value that contains a long run of whitespace. One request with 100 KB of spaces blocks the Node.js event loop for several seconds, which causes a denial of service. When the `multiple` option is set, the `email` rule splits the value into addresses with a regular expression that removes whitespace on each side of the separat…
items.summary: A quadratic-time split in Joi email validation allows remote denial of service via long runs of whitespace. Node.js applications using Joi are affected. Upgrade joi to 17.13.9 or 18.3.1 or later.

items.title: @hapi/content: quadratic-time parsing of Content-Disposition parameters allows denial of service
items.snippet: `Content.disposition()` takes quadratic time when a `Content-Disposition` parameter contains a long token without `=`. One unauthenticated multipart request can block the Node.js event loop for several minutes. `Content.disposition()` reads the parameters with a global regular expression in `String.prototype.replace()`: ```js /([^\=\*\s]+)(\*)?\s*\=\s*(?:([^;'"\s]+\'[\w-]*\'[^;\s]+)|(?:\"([^"]*)\…
items.summary: Quadratic-time parsing of Content-Disposition parameters in @hapi/content allows denial of service via unauthenticated multipart requests. Node.js applications parsing HTTP requests are affected. Upgrade @hapi/content to 6.0.3 or later.

items.title: Glob: AbortSignal cancellation bypass allows post-timeout filesystem traversal
items.snippet: In glob 13.0.6, an aborted async walk rejects or emits an error but continues recursively reading directories in the background. The root cause is that abort branches in src/walker.ts call cb() without returning. As a result, callers that rely on signal or AbortSignal.timeout() to bound glob traversal cost can still incur filesystem I/O and CPU work after the request has already been rejected. Th…
items.summary: An AbortSignal cancellation bypass in glob allows post-timeout filesystem traversal during aborted async walks. Node.js applications using glob are affected. Upgrade glob to 14.0.2 or later.

This is an incomplete fix of CVE-2025-66030. Fixed in node-forge 1.4.1. X.690 section 8.19 encodes the first two arcs of an OID as one subidentifier, `40 * ar…
items.summary: Node-forge fails to range-check the first two arcs of an OID string in asn1.oidToDer, resulting in truncated OID encoding. Applications using node-forge for cryptography are affected. Upgrade node-forge to 1.4.1 or later.

items.title: Forge: Prototype Pollution in forge.http cookie handling via a malicious Set-Cookie
items.snippet: The `forge.http` client stored cookies from `Set-Cookie` response headers in a plain object keyed by cookie name and path. A malicious server could use the cookie name `proto` to add properties to `Object.prototype`, use inherited names such as `constructor` to add properties to `Object`, and send an empty cookie value to delete `Object.prototype` properties. Fixed in node-forge 1.4.1. `client.se…
items.summary: A prototype pollution vulnerability exists in forge.http cookie handling via malicious Set-Cookie headers. Node.js applications parsing HTTP cookies with node-forge are affected. Upgrade node-forge to 1.4.1 or later.

items.title: Forge: TLS client crash when the server sends no certificate
items.snippet: The forge TLS client's check for a missing server certificate read the wrong property and never ran. A malicious TLS server, or an on-path attacker who removes the server's Certificate message, can make `connection.process()` throw a `TypeError`, which crashes applications that use the forge TLS client. Fixed in node-forge 1.4.1. After ServerHelloDone, `tls.handleServerHelloDone()` in `lib/tls.js…
items.summary: The forge TLS client crashes with a TypeError when the server sends no certificate. Applications using node-forge TLS connections are affected. Upgrade node-forge to 1.4.1 or later.

items.title: Forge: Regular expression denial of service in PEM decoding (pem.decode)
items.snippet: `pem.decode()`, which every node-forge API that parses PEM input uses, split messages with a regular expression that takes polynomial time on input without a matching END line, and parsed encapsulated headers with regular expressions that take quadratic time on long header lines. A remote attacker can block the Node.js event loop for seconds to minutes with a crafted input of a few tens of kiloby…
items.summary: A regular expression denial of service vulnerability in pem.decode allows remote attacks via crafted PEM input. Applications using node-forge for PEM parsing are affected. Upgrade node-forge to 1.4.1 or later.

items.title: Forge: Denial of Service via infinite loop in BigInteger.modInverse() with negative input (incomplete fix of CVE-2026-33891)
items.snippet: `BigInteger.prototype.modInverse()` in node-forge's bundled jsbn library enters an infinite loop when the value or the modulus is negative, for example when a negative public exponent is passed to `forge.pki.rsa.generateKeyPair()`. This is an incomplete fix of CVE-2026-33891 (GHSA-5m6q-g25r-mvwx), which handled only a zero value. Fixed in node-forge 1.4.1. `bnModInverse()` (`lib/jsbn.js`, exposed…
items.summary: An infinite loop in BigInteger.modInverse() with negative input allows denial of service in node-forge. Applications generating RSA keys or handling negative numbers are affected. Upgrade node-forge to 1.4.1 or later.

items.title: Forge: verifyCertificateChain() removes trusted CA certificates with the same subject from the CA store
items.snippet: When a CA store created by `pki.createCaStore()` holds two or more certificates with the same subject name, `pki.verifyCertificateChain()` permanently removes those certificates from the store while trying each one as the issuer. A peer can send any certificate that names that subject as its issuer to make all later verifications against those CA certificates fail. Fixed in node-forge 1.4.1. `pki…
items.summary: Certificate chain verification in node-forge permanently removes trusted CA certificates sharing the same subject name from the CA store. Applications verifying certificates are affected. Upgrade node-forge to 1.4.1 or later.

items.title: Forge: AES-GCM authentication bypass via unvalidated tagLength option
items.snippet: The AES-GCM mode in forge.cipher does not validate the tagLength option passed to start(). With a tagLength of 0 or a value that converts to 0 (such as null, false, '' or '0'), the authentication tag is empty, and decipher.finish() returns true for any ciphertext and additional data when the supplied tag is empty or missing. Fixed in node-forge 1.4.1. `modes.gcm.prototype.start()` in `lib/cipherM…
items.summary: An AES-GCM authentication bypass occurs in node-forge when tagLength is set to an invalid or zero value. Applications using forge encryption are affected. Upgrade node-forge to 1.4.1 or later.

items.title: Forge: PKCS#12 MAC forgery and constant-key PBE via zero iteration count
items.snippet: forge.pkcs12.pkcs12FromAsn1() accepts a PKCS#12 MAC iteration count of zero (or less) from the input, and the PKCS#12 key derivation function then returns a constant key that does not depend on the password or salt. An attacker who does not know the password can modify a PKCS#12/PFX file and compute a MAC that verifies with any password; PKCS#12 PBE-encrypted private keys prepared the same way de…
items.summary: PKCS#12 MAC forgery and constant-key PBE can occur due to zero iteration count handling in node-forge. Applications parsing PFX files are affected. Upgrade node-forge to 1.4.1 or later.

items.title: Forge: Denial of service in TLS record processing via a record interleaved with a fragmented handshake message
items.snippet: A connection created with `forge.tls.createConnection()` throws an uncaught `TypeError` from `process()` when it receives a record of another content type while waiting for the rest of a handshake message that was split across records. A peer can trigger this with 18 bytes before the handshake, without authentication, which terminates Node.js processes that use the documented socket wiring. Fixed…
items.summary: A denial of service vulnerability in TLS record processing via interleaved records causes uncaught TypeErrors in node-forge. Applications using forge TLS are affected. Upgrade node-forge to 1.4.1 or later.

items.title: Forge: Denial of service in TLS record processing via call stack exhaustion
items.snippet: Connections created with `forge.tls.createConnection()` processed received TLS records recursively, one stack level per record. A peer can send one chunk of thousands of small records, such as heartbeat records, which are accepted before the handshake, and `process()` throws `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`, which terminates Node.js processes that use the documented socket wiring. F…
items.summary: Call stack exhaustion causes denial of service in TLS record processing in node-forge. Applications handling incoming TLS streams are affected. Upgrade node-forge to 1.4.1 or later.

items.title: Forge: X.509 basicConstraints bypass in verifyCertificateChain() via deprecated extension OIDs 2.5.29.10 and 2.5.29.13
items.snippet: node-forge parses certificate extensions with the deprecated OIDs `2.5.29.10` and `2.5.29.13` as `basicConstraints`, and `forge.pki.verifyCertificateChain()` used the first extension with that name. A certificate with a forged deprecated-OID extension (`cA` TRUE) before its genuine `basicConstraints` extension (`cA` FALSE) is accepted as a CA certificate, and the same technique can hide a `pathLe…
items.summary: An X.509 basicConstraints verification bypass via deprecated extension OIDs allows certificate validation flaws in node-forge. Applications validating certificates are affected. Upgrade node-forge to 1.4.1 or later.

items.title: Nuxt dev server exposes generated appSecret through Vite file serving
items.snippet: When no `appSecret` is configured (via `NUXT_APP_SECRET`, `NITRO_APP_SECRET` or `runtimeConfig.appSecret`), `nuxt dev` generates a development secret and stores it in ` /app-secret` (by default `.nuxt/app-secret`). The build directory is inside the directories that Nuxt passes to Vite's `server.fs.allow`, so the file can be fetched from the dev server: ```bash curl http:// /_nuxt/@fs/ /.nuxt/app-…
items.summary: Nuxt dev server exposes generated appSecret files through Vite file serving when no secret is explicitly configured. Local developers running Nuxt are affected. Upgrade @nuxt/vite-builder to 4.6.3 or later.

items.title: Nuxt: Dot segments in the request path bypass `server/middleware` path checks and server route rules on page routes
items.snippet: Since `4.6.0`, Nuxt resolves `.` and `..` segments in the request path, including percent-encoded forms such as `%2e`, before rendering a page. Nitro's routing, Nitro's route rules and `server/middleware` see the path with those segments still in place. A request for `/%2e/admin` therefore renders the page at `/admin`, while server-side checks keyed on `/admin` do not apply. An unauthenticated at…
items.summary: Dot segments in request paths bypass Nuxt server/middleware path checks and route rules. Nuxt applications handling path-based access control are affected. Upgrade nuxt and @nuxt/nitro-server to 4.6.3 or later.

items.title: Nuxt dev server arbitrary file read through client error reports
items.snippet: A client that can connect to the dev server's HMR socket can send a `nuxt:dev:client-error` event whose message ends in an absolute file path. The dev server reads that file while building the error report, and its contents are returned in the error overlay, on the dev error channel, and in the report shown in the terminal. This affects the development server only; production builds contain none…
items.summary: Nuxt dev server allows arbitrary file reads through client error reports sent over the HMR socket. Developers running Nuxt in development mode are affected. Upgrade @nuxt/vite-builder to 4.6.3 or later.

items.title: Nuxt dev server exposes private runtime config through the Nitro dev bundle
items.snippet: With Nitro 2 (the default server engine in Nuxt 3 and Nuxt 4), the Nitro development server bundle written by `nuxt dev` can be fetched through the Vite dev server. Nitro inlines the resolved `runtimeConfig` into that bundle, so private runtime config values that were resolved at build time can be read by anyone with HTTP access to the dev server. `nuxt dev` writes the Nitro development server bu…
items.summary: Nuxt dev server exposes private runtime config values through the Nitro dev bundle fetched via Vite. Developers running Nuxt dev servers are affected. Upgrade @nuxt/vite-builder to 4.6.3 or later.

items.title: @sigstore/oci sends the registry Authorization header to a cross-host blob-upload Location
items.snippet: @sigstore/oci sends the registry Authorization header to a cross-host blob-upload Location - Confirmed on sigstore-js at `3a83271` (current HEAD). - File: `packages/oci/src/registry.ts`. - `signIn()` installs the credential as a DEFAULT header on the shared client: `this.#fetch = this.#fetch.defaults({ headers: { [HEADER_AUTHORIZATION]: 'Basic ' + basicAuth } })` (`:126-128`) or `... 'Bearer ' +…
items.summary: @sigstore/oci leaks registry Authorization headers to cross-host blob-upload locations. Node.js applications using sigstore are affected. Upgrade @sigstore/oci to 0.7.2 or later.

items.title: follow-redirects: Cross-realm sensitiveHeaders arrays are discarded and custom credentials can follow redirects
items.snippet: follow-redirects 1.16.0 and 1.16.1 validate the documented sensitiveHeaders option with instanceof Array. An array created in another JavaScript realm is silently replaced with an empty list, so a caller-declared custom credential header can be forwarded to an attacker-controlled cross-origin redirect destination. Affected versions The sensitiveHeaders option was introduced in 1.16.0. Published 1…
items.summary: Cross-realm sensitiveHeaders arrays are discarded in follow-redirects, allowing custom credentials to follow redirects to cross-origin destinations. Node.js applications handling HTTP redirects are affected. Upgrade follow-redirects to 1.16.2 or later.

items.title: signalk-server has SSRF via absolute signalk.appIcon URL in the app store icon fetcher
items.snippet: The app store icon code (`dist/appstore/icon-probe.js` around line 200 and `icon-bytes.js` around line 138) resolves a plugin's declared `signalk.appIcon`. Relative paths are pinned to the CDN, but an absolute http(s) URL is used as-is: the server fetches it, follows redirects, and stores any `image/*` response as the plugin's icon, which is then served to the admin UI. Unrelated to GHSA-q59x-jc9…
items.summary: Signal K server is vulnerable to Server-Side Request Forgery via absolute appIcon URLs in the app store icon fetcher. Node.js IoT deployments using Signal K are affected. Upgrade signalk-server to 2.34.0 or later.

items.title: Signal K resources API path traversal can disclose the JWT signing secret and enable remote code execution
items.snippet: Path traversal in the Signal K resources and applicationData APIs lets an unauthenticated or low-privileged user read, write and delete files outside the storage root. Reading /security.json discloses the JWT signing secret, enabling admin token forgery and remote code execution. The v2 REST resources API `GET /signalk/v2/api/resources/:resourceType/:resourceId` passes `resourceId` to `FileStore.…
items.summary: Path traversal in Signal K resources API discloses the JWT signing secret, enabling remote code execution. Node.js IoT server deployments are affected. Upgrade signalk-server to 2.34.0 and @signalk/resources-provider to 1.5.3 or later.

items.title: PHPUnit vulnerable to code execution by other local users via shared temporary directory in PHPT code coverage handling
items.snippet: When PHPT tests are run with code coverage, PHPUnit 13.4.0 to 13.4.3 writes the code of each PHPT test to a directory with a fixed name below the operating system's path used for temporary files, for instance `/tmp/phpunit-phpt` on Linux, and executes it from there. PHPUnit uses this directory even when it was created by another user. On a system where the path used for temporary files is shared…
items.summary: PHPUnit code coverage handling writes PHPT test code to predictable temporary directories, allowing local code execution by other system users. PHP developers running test suites on shared servers are affected. Upgrade phpunit/phpunit to 13.4.4 or later.

items.title: pypdf has possible infinite loop when hitting EOF in standard xref table during trailer search
items.snippet: An attacker who uses this vulnerability can craft a PDF which leads to an infinite loop. This requires opening an incomplete file without a `trailer`. This has been fixed in [pypdf==6.21.4](https://github.com/py-pdf/pypdf/releases/tag/6.21.4). If you cannot upgrade yet, consider applying the changes from PR [#4289](https://github.com/py-pdf/pypdf/pull/4289).
items.summary: An infinite loop vulnerability in pypdf occurs when encountering EOF in standard xref tables during trailer search. Python applications processing malformed PDFs are affected. Upgrade pypdf to 6.21.4 or later.

items.title: pypdf has possible large memory usage when parsing page tree
items.snippet: An attacker who uses this vulnerability can craft a PDF which leads to large memory usage. This requires parsing the page tree with many shared resources. This has been fixed in [pypdf==6.21.4](https://github.com/py-pdf/pypdf/releases/tag/6.21.4). If you cannot upgrade yet, consider applying the changes from PR [#4290](https://github.com/py-pdf/pypdf/pull/4290).
items.summary: Large memory usage vulnerability in pypdf occurs when parsing page trees with many shared resources. Python applications processing complex PDFs are affected. Upgrade pypdf to 6.21.4 or later.

items.title: pypdf has possible infinite loop when cloning dictionaries
items.snippet: An attacker who uses this vulnerability can craft a PDF which leads to an infinite loop. This requires cloning/duplicating a `DictionaryObject`. This has been fixed in [pypdf==6.21.4](https://github.com/py-pdf/pypdf/releases/tag/6.21.4). If you cannot upgrade yet, consider applying the changes from PR [#4288](https://github.com/py-pdf/pypdf/pull/4288).
items.summary: An infinite loop in pypdf occurs when cloning DictionaryObjects from crafted PDFs. Python applications duplicating PDF dictionary objects are affected. Upgrade pypdf to 6.21.4 or later.

items.title: Authlib RFC 7592 examples omit registration-access-token client binding
items.snippet: RFC 7592 (OAuth 2.0 Dynamic Client Registration Management Protocol) lets a previously registered client read, update, or delete its own registration, authenticated by a `registration_access_token` issued specifically to that client at registration time. The entire security model of this protocol depends on the server verifying that the token presented in the request actually belongs to the clien…
items.summary: Authlib client registration management examples omit registration-access-token client bindings per RFC 7592. Python applications implementing OAuth 2.0 dynamic registration are affected. Upgrade Authlib to 1.9.1 or later.

items.title: pypdf has possible long runtimes when retrieving page labels
items.snippet: An attacker who uses this vulnerability can craft a PDF which leads to large runtimes. This requires retrieving the page labels of a file. This has been fixed in [pypdf==6.21.3](https://github.com/py-pdf/pypdf/releases/tag/6.21.3). If you cannot upgrade yet, consider applying the changes from PR [#4251](https://github.com/py-pdf/pypdf/pull/4251).
items.summary: Long runtimes occur in pypdf when retrieving page labels from crafted PDF files. Python applications processing page labels are affected. Upgrade pypdf to 6.21.3 or later.

items.title: pypdf has possible large memory usage for exceptions in strict mode
items.snippet: An attacker who uses this vulnerability can craft a PDF which leads to large memory usage. This requires loading an invalid dictionary. This has been fixed in [pypdf==6.21.3](https://github.com/py-pdf/pypdf/releases/tag/6.21.3). If you cannot upgrade yet, consider applying the changes from PR [#4265](https://github.com/py-pdf/pypdf/pull/4265).
items.summary: Large memory usage occurs in pypdf strict mode when loading invalid dictionaries. Python applications parsing untrusted PDF files are affected. Upgrade pypdf to 6.21.3 or later.

items.title: pypdf has possible long runtimes/large memory usage for encrypted PDF files
items.snippet: An attacker who uses this vulnerability can craft a PDF which leads to large runtimes/memory usage. This requires accessing the page count of an encrypted PDF file, which itself declares a wrong `/Count` value. This has been fixed in [pypdf==6.21.3](https://github.com/py-pdf/pypdf/releases/tag/6.21.3). If you cannot upgrade yet, consider applying the changes from PR [#4270](https://github.com/py-…
items.summary: pypdf allows a crafted PDF file to cause excessive runtimes and memory usage when accessing page counts. Python developers processing user PDFs are affected. Upgrade pypdf to 6.21.3 or later.

items.title: pypdf has possible large memory usage when parsing cross-reference streams
items.snippet: An attacker who uses this vulnerability can craft a PDF which leads to large memory usage. This requires opening a file with cross-reference streams. This has been fixed in [pypdf==6.21.3](https://github.com/py-pdf/pypdf/releases/tag/6.21.3). If you cannot upgrade yet, consider applying the changes from PR [#4269](https://github.com/py-pdf/pypdf/pull/4269).
items.summary: pypdf has a potential large memory usage vulnerability when parsing cross-reference streams in PDFs. Python developers handling untrusted PDF files are affected. Upgrade pypdf to 6.21.3 or later.

items.title: pyasn1 has quadratic CPU consumption in constructed BIT STRING decoding
items.snippet: In pyasn1 through 0.6.4, decoding a constructed BIT STRING with many fragments repeatedly shifts and copies the entire value accumulated so far. For fixed-size fragments, CPU time grows quadratically with the encoded input size. An application that passes sufficiently large, attacker-controlled ASN.1 data to an affected decoder can suffer CPU exhaustion during `decode()`; no conversion or formatt…
items.summary: pyasn1 suffers from quadratic CPU consumption during constructed BIT STRING decoding. Python applications processing attacker-controlled ASN.1 data are affected. Upgrade pyasn1 to 0.6.5 or later.

items.title: pyasn1 has quadratic-complexity denial of service in binary REAL decoding
items.snippet: In pyasn1 0.6.4 and earlier, decoding a binary-encoded ASN.1 REAL with a large mantissa can consume CPU time quadratic in the mantissa length. The BER, CER, and DER decoders all use the affected `RealPayloadDecoder`. An application is exposed when it passes attacker-controlled ASN.1 containing a REAL value to one of these decoders, either without an `asn1Spec` or with a schema that includes REAL.…
items.summary: pyasn1 has a quadratic-complexity denial of service vulnerability in binary REAL decoding. Python apps decoding ASN.1 REAL data with large mantissas are affected. Upgrade pyasn1 to 0.6.5 or later.

items.title: pyasn1 has quadratic-time denial of service in constructed string and indefinite-length ANY decoding
items.snippet: In pyasn1 0.6.4 and earlier, decoding a constructed OCTET STRING or character string made of many fragments can spend disproportionate CPU time repeatedly copying the accumulated value. A separate indefinite-length `ANY` path has the same problem while collecting the encoded components. The work grows roughly quadratically with the number of fixed-size fragments, although the input and decoded va…
items.summary: pyasn1 suffers from quadratic-time denial of service during constructed string and indefinite-length ANY decoding. Python services parsing complex fragmentized strings are affected. Upgrade pyasn1 to 0.6.5 or later.

items.title: pyasn1 has quadratic CPU use in schemaless BER/CER/DER container decoding
items.snippet: When an application decodes attacker-controlled BER, CER, or DER data without an ASN.1 schema, a container with many distinct long tag IDs can cause quadratic CPU use. Repeated inputs can exhaust CPU and reduce service availability. ConstructedPayloadDecoderBase._decodeComponentsSchemaless inserts every decoded component’s TagSet into a growing set, although it only needs to distinguish one tag s…
items.summary: pyasn1 has quadratic CPU usage in schemaless BER, CER, and DER container decoding. Python apps decoding arbitrary inputs without a schema are affected. Upgrade pyasn1 to 0.6.5 or later.

items.title: GraphQL-core has denial of service via memory leak in aborted validations
items.snippet: When a validation was aborted because the document contained more errors than allowed by `max_errors` (100 by default), `validate()` raised a single module-level `ValidationAbortedError` instance. Python appends the frames of every `raise` to the existing `traceback` of an exception that is raised again, so every aborted validation extended the traceback of this shared error. That traceback kept…
items.summary: GraphQL-core contains a denial of service vulnerability via memory leak in aborted validations. Python applications processing heavy or invalid GraphQL documents are affected. Upgrade graphql-core to 3.3.1 or later.

items.title: OAuthLib: Token grants can use attacker-supplied client_id for authorization after authenticating a different client
items.snippet: OAuthlib's token grant handlers can authenticate one client while authorizing the grant type and requested scopes using a different, attacker-supplied `client_id` from the request body. In affected token grant flows, `authenticate_client(request)` sets `request.client` to the authenticated client object, but OAuthlib does not require `request.client_id` to match `request.client.client_id`. If the…
items.summary: OAuthLib token grant handlers can mix client authentication and authorization using an attacker-supplied client_id. Python developers building OAuth providers are affected. Upgrade oauthlib to 4.0.0 or later.

items.title: E-Maj 5.0.1: Major Security Update.
items.snippet: We are very glad to announce the E-Maj 5.0.1 version. E-Maj is a PostgreSQL extension which enables fine-grained write logging and time travel on subsets of the database. This version mainly fixes a vulnerability encountered in all previous versions, allowing some users to gain superuser privileges under certain circumstances. Users are strongly encouraged to update their installed version as soo…
items.summary: E-Maj 5.0.1 fixes a privilege escalation vulnerability in all previous versions that allowed users to gain superuser privileges. Upgrade E-Maj to 5.0.1 or later.

items.title: pgAdmin 4 v9.19 Released
items.snippet: The pgAdmin Development Team is pleased to announce pgAdmin 4 version 9.19. For more details please see the release notes. pgAdmin is the leading open-source graphical management tool for PostgreSQL. For more information, please see the webs…
items.summary: pgAdmin 4 v9.19 fixes 15 security vulnerabilities along with bug fixes. Upgrade pgAdmin to v9.19 or later.
